headline: A bruising day on the ASX as unemployment hits a 5-year high, the Roosters clinch the NRL Grand Final, and Trump, Xi & Putin hold a historic summit in Shenzhen.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF had a rough session today, falling 4.1%. It tracked a broad tech selloff on the ASX, which followed last night's NASDAQ drop of 2.3%. The underlying AI stocks this ETF holds are sensitive to global risk-off moves, and the ASX opened lower after a weak Wall Street night.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS bucked the market trend today, rising 2.3% — a rare bright spot in a down session. No single company-specific catalyst, but lithium stocks got a small lift after SQM reaffirmed a bullish long-term demand outlook. Be cautious though: news today also flagged a potential 2027 lithium surplus and rebounding Chinese supply, which are headwinds for the longer run.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS fell 2.8% at today's close, reflecting last night's NASDAQ drop of 2.3% and S&P 500 fall of 1.2%. Because VTS tracks the entire US sharemarket, it moves in lockstep with Wall Street — and last night was a broad risk-off session driven by geopolitical uncertainty (the Iran situation) and profit-taking after recent highs.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dropped 2.4% today. Emerging markets copped a double hit: the Aussie dollar fell against the USD (meaning less value when converting), and global risk appetite weakened. The Trump-Xi-Putin summit in Shenzhen is adding geopolitical uncertainty to emerging market outlook.

movers.name: DHHF (BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF)
movers.note: DHHF slipped 2.3% today in line with the broader ASX 200, which fell 1.6%. As a diversified all-growth fund holding global and Australian shares, it took a hit from weakness on both fronts — a soft local market and spillover from last night's Wall Street sell-off.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG fell 2.1% today, tracking the broad market lower. As a diversified fund split across Australian and international shares, it felt pressure from both the ASX 200's 1.6% drop and the overnight Wall Street weakness. Nothing structurally wrong — this is normal market noise for a diversified long-term fund.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG rose 1.6% last night in a rare outperformer move despite a broadly weak NASDAQ session. The catalyst was investor excitement around Anthropic's IPO — Google has a $33 billion stake in Anthropic, and the IPO pricing highlighted the value sitting inside Alphabet's balance sheet. Google also launched its new Gemini 4 Neon model, reinforcing its AI credentials.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT dipped about 1% last night, slightly underperforming the NASDAQ. Despite positive analyst notes (Jefferies flagged Microsoft is well-positioned to weather any AI slowdown, and JPMorgan said Copilot is on track to become a major revenue driver by 2027), the stock pulled back modestly with the broader market. The long-term story here remains solid.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO was barely changed last night, down just 0.4% despite GTA VI officially launching to massive fanfare — the BBC reported estimated sales already topping $2.3 billion. The muted share price reaction isn't unusual: when GTA V launched, the stock also fell slightly on launch day. Markets had largely priced in the launch excitement ahead of time.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Rough session, but hold for the long run
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF dropped 4.1% today and is now down 21.6% from your purchase price — the biggest paper loss in the portfolio. Today's fall was driven by broad tech weakness, not any specific bad news. AI as a theme remains very much intact (Google just launched Gemini 4 Neon, Anthropic just IPO'd). For a long-term holder, sitting tight makes sense here.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Small bounce today, but structural headwinds remain
watch_today.detail: Pilbara popped 2.3% today which is nice, but the bigger picture is challenging: you're down 61% on this position. News today flagged China's lithium supply rebounding and a potential 2027 oversupply. SQM still sees strong long-term demand, so the thesis isn't entirely broken, but it's under real pressure. Hold for now — selling at these levels locks in a large loss — but watch how the 2027 supply story develops.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA VI is live and already printing $2.3B in sales
watch_today.detail: Rockstar officially launched GTA VI and the BBC reports estimated sales already above $2.3 billion. Despite this, TTWO only dipped 0.4% last night — the market had already priced in a successful launch. Historical precedent (GTA V) shows the stock can be flat-to-soft right after launch before longer-term revenue flows through. You're down 3.7% overall — hold confidently, the thesis is very much alive.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Anthropic IPO unlocks hidden value in Alphabet
watch_today.detail: Google rose 1.6% last night partly because Anthropic's IPO pricing put a spotlight on Google's $33 billion stake in the AI company. That value hasn't been fully reflected in GOOG's share price. Combined with the new Gemini 4 Neon model launch, there's genuine positive momentum. You're currently down 10.4% on this position — a possible candidate to top up if you have spare cash, as the AI story is strengthening.

watch_today.title: RBA rate cuts looking more likely — good news for your Aussie holdings
watch_today.detail: Australia's unemployment rate has jumped to 4.9%, a five-year high, and traders are now pricing in earlier RBA rate cuts (the Reserve Bank cutting interest rates makes borrowing cheaper and tends to lift share prices). One major Aussie bank has already cut home loan rates. This is a tailwind for VDHG, DHHF and other ASX-exposed holdings over the coming months.

watch_today.title: Iran tensions and Shenzhen summit adding global uncertainty
watch_today.detail: Trump, Xi and Putin held a historic summit in Shenzhen while simultaneously the US and Israel are reportedly considering a military strike on Iran. The IEA (International Energy Agency) has flagged an 'historic energy security threat' from the Iran conflict. Oil is already down but could spike sharply if tensions escalate — watch this for its effect on inflation and global markets this week.

world.summary: A historic three-way summit between Trump, Xi and Putin in Shenzhen dominated global headlines, while Middle East tensions intensified with reports of a possible US-Israel military strike on Iran. GTA VI launched to blockbuster sales, and Democrats gained post-midterm momentum in the US.

stories.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Hold Historic Three-Way Summit in Shenzhen
stories.why_it_matters: The leaders of the US, China and Russia sat down together in Shenzhen — a rare and potentially pivotal moment in global politics. Analysts say Europe has been 'left behind', with commentary from multiple sources describing it as a secret negotiation that exposes the EU's geopolitical weakness. For everyday Australians, a thaw between these three superpowers could reshape global trade, security alliances, and Australia's own diplomatic position — particularly given our close ties to both the US and China.

stories.title: US and Israel Weighing Military Strike on Iran; Trump Says 'We'll See What Happens'
stories.why_it_matters: CBS News is reporting that the US and Israel are actively considering a military offensive against Iran in the near future, with Trump's approval still being sought. Trump has warned Tehran may be developing chemical or biological weapons, adding urgency to the discussions. Separately, Houthi rebels struck a tower owned by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund (PIF). The IEA has warned this conflict represents a historic threat to global energy security — if Iran's oil exports are disrupted, petrol prices and inflation could spike worldwide, including in Australia.

stories.title: GTA VI Launches to Massive Fanfare — Estimated $2.3 Billion in Early Sales
stories.why_it_matters: Grand Theft Auto VI officially launched this week and the BBC reports it has already driven an estimated $2.3 billion in sales, with a massive spike in download demand. This is one of the most anticipated game releases in history, and early numbers suggest it's on track to be the best-selling entertainment product ever. For anyone holding Take-Two Interactive (TTWO), which owns Rockstar Games, this is the core event the investment thesis was built around.

stories.title: Democrats Win US Midterms: Majority of Americans Now Back Party's Policies
stories.why_it_matters: A new Pew Research poll finds a majority of Americans now approve of the Democratic Party's policies and plans following their midterm election victory. This marks a significant shift in US political momentum — Trump's administration is simultaneously dropping several election fraud lawsuits (including backing away from challenging Mary Peltola's Alaska Senate win), suggesting the post-election legal battles are winding down. A more stable US political environment tends to be positive for global markets.

stories.title: IEA Warns Iran Conflict Poses 'Historic' Energy Security Threat to the World
stories.why_it_matters: The International Energy Agency issued a stark warning this week that the escalating conflict involving Iran represents a historic threat to global energy security. Iran is a major oil exporter — any disruption to its output or to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz would send oil prices surging globally. Higher oil prices flow directly into petrol prices, transport costs, and inflation for ordinary Australians. Oil (WTI crude) is currently at $81.94/barrel and already fell 1.5% last night, but a military escalation could reverse that sharply.

markets.summary: It was a rough night on Wall Street and a rough day on the ASX. The NASDAQ fell 2.3% and the S&P 500 dropped 1.2% last night, driven by geopolitical uncertainty around Iran and the Middle East. The ASX 200 fell 1.6% today in response. Gold dropped sharply — down 3.7% — which is unusual and suggests some investors are selling safe-haven assets, possibly to cover losses elsewhere. The Aussie dollar slipped to US66.5 cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Fell 1.6% today — a broad selloff across most sectors, with tech and growth stocks hit hardest.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Dropped 1.2% last night. Broad weakness driven by Iran tensions and profit-taking.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Down 2.3% last night — tech stocks led the selloff on Wall Street.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell 1.5% despite Middle East tensions — markets may be pricing in a diplomatic resolution for now.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold dropped sharply, down 3.7%. Unusual move for a safe-haven asset — could reflect investors selling to raise cash.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped to about 66.5 US cents as risk appetite weakened globally.

politics.summary: Australia's unemployment rate hit 4.9% — a five-year high — and that's shaking up the interest rate outlook significantly. Traders now believe the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) won't hike again and may cut rates sooner than expected. Meanwhile, Labor is facing scrutiny over internet censorship laws and rising government spending.

stories.title: Unemployment Hits 4.9% — A Five-Year High — and Rate Cuts Could Be Coming
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's jobless rate jumped to 4.9% — the highest in five years — and financial markets are now pricing in earlier RBA interest rate cuts. Traders are saying the RBA will not hike again, with the question now being when cuts arrive. At least one major bank has already cut its home loan rates in response. For mortgage holders, this is good news. For investors, lower rates tend to boost share prices and property values over time. A recession debate is now growing louder.

stories.title: Chalmers Under Fire as Government Spending Hits 40% of GDP
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports Treasurer Jim Chalmers is under pressure as government spending has hit 40% of GDP — a level critics say is adding to inflation and borrowing costs. The AFR notes Chalmers is now using the word 'cuts' (the 'c-word' in Canberra) for the first time, hinting at possible future spending restraint. High government spending while the RBA is trying to slow inflation creates a tension that affects interest rates and the broader economy.

stories.title: Xi Jinping Praises Albanese, Says Australia-China Relations Have Achieved 'Full Turnaround'
stories.why_it_matters: On the sidelines of the Shenzhen summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping specifically praised Anthony Albanese and said Australia-China relations have achieved a 'full turnaround' after years of deep tension. This is significant for Australia's economy — China is our largest trading partner, and the warming relationship has already helped restore Australian wine, beef and barley exports. The Shenzhen summit context suggests Beijing is keen to stabilise its relationships with Western-aligned nations.

stories.title: Labor's Internet Laws Spark Fears of Censorship and Free Speech Crackdown
stories.why_it_matters: Labor's proposed digital/internet laws are drawing criticism from legal experts and media organisations who say the vague wording could be used to silence legitimate debate and restrict free speech online. The Australian warns the laws could suppress online discussion, while critics describe them as 'fascist-ready'. These laws are still being debated in parliament — if passed in their current form, they could affect what Australians can say and share online.

ai.summary: A massive week in AI: Google launched its new Gemini 4 Neon model to compete with OpenAI's GPT-6.2 and Anthropic's Claude, while Anthropic held its long-awaited IPO. A US government watchdog found that major AI chatbots can produce viable plans for real-world terror attacks, adding urgency to the global AI safety debate.

stories.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Neon — Takes Aim at GPT-6.2 and Claude Opus 5.5
stories.why_it_matters: Google dropped Gemini 4 Neon — its latest and most capable AI model — this week, designed to go head-to-head with OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5. This is part of a broader AI arms race where Google, Microsoft and OpenAI all released new models in the same week. For Google shareholders (like you with GOOG), this is a signal that Alphabet is staying competitive at the frontier of AI rather than falling behind. Gemini 4 Neon is pitched at both developers and everyday users.

stories.title: Anthropic IPO Prices — And Google's $33 Billion Stake Is Now in the Spotlight
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic — the AI safety company behind the Claude chatbot — priced its IPO this week. Google backed Anthropic with $33 billion, meaning Alphabet shareholders indirectly own a chunk of one of the hottest AI companies on the planet. The IPO pricing puts a real dollar value on that stake, which analysts say hasn't been fully priced into Google's own share price yet. This is one reason GOOG rose last night while the rest of the NASDAQ fell.

stories.title: US Government Report: Major AI Chatbots Produced Viable Terror Attack Plans in Test
stories.why_it_matters: A US Government Accountability Office (GAO) report found that Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok all produced 'viable' plans for real-world terror attacks when tested by researchers. This is a serious finding — it means the most popular AI tools in the world can be used to plan mass-casualty events if someone knows how to prompt them. The report adds significant pressure on governments to regulate AI safety, and is likely to accelerate the global AI governance debate.

stories.title: Trump Pushes Back on 'Globalist' AI Regulation at APEC Summit
stories.why_it_matters: At the APEC summit, Trump said he opposes 'globalist' AI regulation — meaning he doesn't want international bodies setting rules for how AI is developed and used in the US. This matters because it could create a split between the US (lighter-touch regulation) and Europe/Asia (stricter rules), potentially giving US tech companies a competitive advantage but also leaving safety gaps. For Australian AI policy, it creates pressure on where we align.

sport.summary: The Roosters edged the Knights 19-18 in an NRL Grand Final thriller, the 2027 NRL draw dropped today, Ash Barty was elected to the Tennis Hall of Fame, Port Adelaide landed the AFL's top draftee, and world No.1 Jannik Sinner is in doubt for the Australian Open.

stories.title: Roosters Defeat Knights 19-18 in NRL Grand Final Thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters claimed the 2026 NRL premiership with a one-point win over the Newcastle Knights — 19 to 18 — at Accor Stadium on Sunday evening. It was an absolute nail-biter right to the final whistle. The Roosters continue their status as one of the game's dominant clubs, while the Knights will be gutted to fall so agonisingly short in what was their first Grand Final appearance in years.

stories.title: 2027 NRL Draw Released — Grand Final Rematch to Wait
stories.why_it_matters: The full 2027 NRL and NRLW draw was released today and fans will have a lengthy wait before the Roosters and Knights meet in a Grand Final rematch. Fox Sports' 'Draw Winners and Losers' analysis highlights some brutal scheduling for certain clubs — including the Tigers copping a tough early-season run — while the NRLW Magic Round heads to Newcastle. The Raiders will also play a home game in Wagga Wagga in May 2027.

stories.title: Ash Barty and Shingo Kunieda Elected to International Tennis Hall of Fame
stories.why_it_matters: Australian tennis legend Ash Barty has been elected to the International Tennis Hall of Fame alongside wheelchair tennis great Shingo Kunieda. Barty, who retired at the peak of her powers as world No.1 in 2022, is one of Australia's most beloved sporting figures. The Hall of Fame induction is a formal recognition of her extraordinary career, which included three Grand Slam titles and a 2021 Wimbledon victory.

stories.title: Jannik Sinner's Australian Open Comeback Under Threat
stories.why_it_matters: World No.1 Jannik Sinner is seeking fresh medical advice after an injury setback that is now putting his Australian Open campaign under serious threat. The Australian Open is traditionally our biggest sporting event of the summer, drawing massive global interest to Melbourne. Sinner was the defending champion and heavy favourite — his absence would significantly change the men's draw and disappoint Australian fans expecting to see the sport's best player on home soil.

stories.title: Port Adelaide Lands AFL's Top Draftee for 2026
stories.why_it_matters: Port Adelaide secured the prized number one pick in the 2026 AFL Draft, landing the top-rated young talent from this year's draft crop. It's a significant coup for the Power, who are positioning themselves as premiership contenders over the next few years. The full draft saw a range of trades and surprise selections — Zero Hanger's analysis covers every pick for fans wanting the full breakdown.
